excerpt: Pomelo combined international money transfer with a credit card, letting US senders pay for remittances to the Philippines on credit and build credit history. Zepz, owner of WorldRemit and Sendwave, acquired it in January 2026.
content:
Pomelo was a San Francisco fintech that built a credit card for sending money home. Instead of paying for a remittance from a bank account or with an expensive cash advance, a customer in the United States could send money to family abroad using the Pomelo Mastercard, then repay over time, while the payments helped build their US credit history. Its product was aimed mainly at migrants sending money to the Philippines. Pomelo said customers could also earn points on purchases and transfers, CFOtech reported. TechCrunch described the model as "send now, pay later".

Pomelo was founded by Eric Velasquez Frenkiel, its CEO. Its product launched in the Philippines in 2022. TechCrunch reported a $20 million seed round led by Founders Fund in 2022, and in April 2024 a $35 million Series A led by Vy Capital, a Dubai-based investment firm. Keith Rabois sat on Pomelo's board, and Kevin Hartz, a co-founder of Eventbrite and the money transfer service Xoom, was also a backer.

Acquired by Zepz. In January 2026 Zepz, the parent company of the remittance brands WorldRemit and Sendwave, announced that it had acquired Pomelo's product and team, Fintech News Philippines and CFOtech reported. Zepz said the deal would help it expand beyond money transfer into cards, lending and credit building for cross-border communities, and called the Philippines one of its core markets. Financial terms were not disclosed. Zepz said Pomelo's product had been temporarily paused for customers while it was integrated into Zepz's roadmap, without giving a date for its return. Pomelo's own website no longer loads.

Because the product is paused, there is nothing to sign up for today. This profile draws on published reporting. We have not used the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

faq.a: Zepz, owner of WorldRemit and Sendwave, acquired its product and team in January 2026 and paused the product while integrating it.
It offered a credit card designed for remittances, letting US senders pay on credit and build credit history while sending money to the Philippines.
A $20 million seed led by Founders Fund in 2022 and a $35 million Series A led by Vy Capital in 2024, TechCrunch reported.
Eric Velasquez Frenkiel, who was CEO.
